intro.data: Chaining boxed steps tends to nest boxes inside boxes — a Maybe holding a Maybe. The monad's other move is 'join': collapse a double box into a single one, KEEPING what's there. One machine merges it faithfully; the other crushes it to nothing. Build the faithful join.
intro.alchemy: Chaining sealed steps tends to nest vials inside vials. The monad's other move is to Decant: pour a vial-of-a-vial into one vial, KEEPING the contents. One apparatus decants faithfully; the other tips it all out. Build the faithful decant.
intro.spellcraft: Chaining bound steps tends to nest charms inside charms. The monad's other move is to Merge: fold a charm-of-a-charm into one, KEEPING the essence. One rune merges faithfully; the other snuffs it out. Build the faithful merge.
intro.abstract: join (μ : T(T(A)) → T(A)) flattens a doubly-wrapped value, preserving content. One candidate is μ; the other collapses to the empty box. Build μ.

goal.data: Flatten the double box, keeping the user inside.
goal.alchemy: Decant the vial-of-vial, keeping the herb.
goal.spellcraft: Merge the charm-of-charm, keeping the rune.
goal.abstract: Send T(T(A)) to T(A) as μ, preserving the value.

afterSuccess.data: 'join' collapsed a box-in-a-box into a single box, keeping the user. That flattening is what makes chaining possible: do a step that returns a box, and join the nesting away. The 'Crush' look-alike had the right type but discarded the contents.
afterSuccess.alchemy: 'Decant' poured the vial-of-vial into one, keeping the herb — the flattening that makes chaining possible. 'Tip Out' had the right type but discarded the contents.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: 'Merge' folded the charm-of-charm into one, keeping the rune — the flattening that makes chaining possible. 'Snuff' had the right type but lost the essence.
afterSuccess.abstract: μ : T(T(A)) → T(A) flattens the nesting, preserving content. With η it is the structure of a monad; bind g = μ ∘ T(g).

reveal.summary: join (μ : T(T(A)) → T(A)) flattens a box-inside-a-box into one box. It's what lets you chain a step that returns a box and not drown in nesting — bind g = join ∘ map(g).
